principle_text: When the persuadee agrees with a general statement but does not show clear donation intent, avoid making vague emotional appeals that do not directly connect to the donation request.
When the persuadee expresses curiosity about your helping methods, avoid giving vague or generic answers that do not guide them toward a specific charitable action.
When the persuadee shows interest in helping others, you should share your own personal experiences to build rapport and encourage further engagement.
When the persuadee shows interest in your helping activities but does not engage further toward donation, avoid giving only factual answers without linking to the donation appeal.
When the persuadee shows interest but does not indicate commitment, avoid asking closed questions that do not advance the conversation toward a donation decision.
When the persuadee expresses confusion or asks for clarification, avoid giving vague or unrelated information that does not directly address their question or connect to the donation appeal.
